---
title: Declaring the Quarto version of a project
---

## Overview

Quarto 2 is not fully backwards compatible with Quarto 1. A project
written for one and rendered by the other can fail, or render with
subtly different output. So every project says which major version of
Quarto it is written for, with one line in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

quarto-required: "^2"
```

`quarto-required` holds a version range. `"^2"` means "any Quarto 2
version". It is the same key Quarto 1 uses, with the same syntax, so
both versions understand it:

- Quarto 2 renders the project without comment.
- Quarto 1 (version 1.4 and later) refuses to render it, with a message
  that its version does not satisfy the range.

Projects created with `q2 create` already carry the line.

## When the declaration is missing

A `_quarto.yml` without `quarto-required` might have been written for a
Quarto 1 release that predates Quarto 2, so Quarto 2 presumes it
belongs to a Quarto 1 project. It still renders the project, but it
warns once per render ([`Q-5-53`](../../errors/project/Q-5-53.qmd)):

```default
Warning [Q-5-53]: `_quarto.yml` does not declare a Quarto version
Without `quarto-required`, `_quarto.yml` is presumed to belong to a Quarto 1 project, and Quarto 1 will render it without complaint.
ℹ If this project is meant for Quarto 2, add `quarto-required: "^2"` to `_quarto.yml`?
```

Under `q2 render --strict` the warning fails the render.

## Ranges that do not target Quarto 2

Quarto 2 also warns about a range that does not single out Quarto 2:

| Range | Example | Warning |
|---|---|---|
| admits Quarto 2 only | `"^2"`, `">=2"` | none |
| admits both Quarto 1 and Quarto 2 | `">=1.4"`, `"*"` | [`Q-5-54`](../../errors/project/Q-5-54.qmd) |
| admits Quarto 1 only, or neither | `"^1.7"`, `"^3"` | [`Q-5-55`](../../errors/project/Q-5-55.qmd) |
| not a version range | `2`, `"two"` | [`Q-5-56`](../../errors/project/Q-5-56.qmd) |

An open range such as `">=1.4"` is the common case: many Quarto 1
projects declare a minimum version that way, and the range says nothing
about which major version the project is written for.

## Only `_quarto.yml` counts

Quarto 2 reads the declaration from the project's own `_quarto.yml`
(or `_quarto.yaml`) and nowhere else. A `quarto-required` in a profile
file (`_quarto-<name>.yml`), in `_quarto.yml.local`, in a
`_metadata.yml`, in a document's front matter, or passed with `-M` does
not declare the project's version.

The version a project is written for is a property of the whole
project, so it lives in the one file that defines the project.

Documents rendered on their own, outside any project, are not checked.

## Silencing the warning

A project that is deliberately left undeclared, for example a Quarto 1
project you also render with Quarto 2 to compare the output, can turn
the warning off in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
diagnostics:
  Q-5-53:
    level: off
    reason: "a Quarto 1 project we render with both versions"
```

The same works for `Q-5-54`, `Q-5-55` and `Q-5-56`. The entry must be
in the project configuration; a `diagnostics:` entry in a document's
front matter does not silence a project-level warning.

## Difference from Quarto 1

Quarto 1 checks `quarto-required` against its own version and stops
the render when the version does not satisfy the range. It reads the
key from each document's merged metadata, so a document's front matter
can override the project's value.

Quarto 2 does not compare the range with its own version. It only asks
whether the range singles out Quarto 2, and only in `_quarto.yml`.
